# Environment variables of the modules

> Generated by `scripts/docs-generate.ts` from the `envVars`, `envServices`, `envOptional` and `envRequiredWhen` fields of every descriptor. Do not edit this file. Run `pnpm docs:generate` to update it.

Every module declares the values it reads in its descriptor. `saasaloy env` collects them into `packages/env/.env`, and each service reads the keys named in its Services column. A key with no declared services falls back to the `PUBLIC_` prefix rule, and the table marks it inferred. An Optional cell such as "required when `EMAIL_PROVIDER=plunk`" marks a conditional key: it may stay blank while that condition is false. The environment of the CLI itself is on [the reference page](../reference.md#environment-variables).

51 variables.

| Variable | Module | Services | Optional | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_COOKIE_PREFIX` | [`auth`](modules/auth.md) | api | yes | Optional, dev only. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. When set and BETTER_AUTH_URL is an http: URL, both session cookies become <prefix>-client.session_token and <prefix>-admin.session_token, so two worktrees on one host keep separate sessions. pnpm dev:ports writes it into apps/api/.env.local in a linked worktree and leaves it out in the main checkout. It is ignored on an https: BETTER_AUTH_URL, so production never reads it. |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | [`auth`](modules/auth.md) | api | yes | Workers secret used to sign sessions. Required: auth throws while the Worker initializes when it is unset, unless BETTER_AUTH_URL names a loopback host. |
| `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | [`auth`](modules/auth.md) | api | no | The API's own origin (e.g. https://api.x.com, or http://localhost:4000 locally). Used as the auth baseURL, to derive the cookie domain, and to allow the keyless local dev loop. When unset there is no loopback exception, so BETTER_AUTH_SECRET becomes mandatory, and the session cookie stays host-only unless COOKIE_DOMAIN sets it. FIRST SUPERADMIN: every sign-up gets role 'user'; no account is promoted automatically. Make the first superadmin before this origin is public: `pnpm db:prod:superadmin --email <you>`. Development databases get one from the seed. |
| `BKASH_APP_KEY` | [`payment-bkash`](modules/payment-bkash.md) | api | required when `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=bkash` | Required while PAYMENT_PROVIDER lists bkash, and may stay blank under any other provider. The app key of your bKash merchant account, from https://developer.bka.sh for the sandbox and from bKash's merchant onboarding for live. Read from apps/api/.env in local dev (saasaloy env, then pnpm env:setup) and from a Workers secret in production. Unset, every bkash call throws PaymentError("invalid_request") naming this key before anything is sent. |
| `BKASH_APP_SECRET` | [`payment-bkash`](modules/payment-bkash.md) | api | required when `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=bkash` | Required while PAYMENT_PROVIDER lists bkash, and may stay blank under any other provider. The app secret issued with the app key. It is sent on the token grant and the token refresh, so a deployed Worker holds it as a secret (`wrangler secret put BKASH_APP_SECRET`), never in wrangler.jsonc. |
| `BKASH_MODE` | [`payment-bkash`](modules/payment-bkash.md) | api | yes | Which gateway host to use: `live` for https://tokenized.pay.bka.sh, anything else for the sandbox at https://tokenized.sandbox.bka.sh. Optional, and it fails safe: only the exact string `live` selects the live gateway, so a typo sends a test payment to the sandbox. |
| `BKASH_PASSWORD` | [`payment-bkash`](modules/payment-bkash.md) | api | required when `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=bkash` | Required while PAYMENT_PROVIDER lists bkash, and may stay blank under any other provider. The merchant API password that goes with the username, sent as the `password` header on the two token calls. A Worker secret for the same reason the app secret is. |
| `BKASH_USERNAME` | [`payment-bkash`](modules/payment-bkash.md) | api | required when `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=bkash` | Required while PAYMENT_PROVIDER lists bkash, and may stay blank under any other provider. The merchant API username, sent as the `username` header on the two token calls. It is not your bKash wallet number and not your portal login. |
| `COOKIE_DOMAIN` | [`auth`](modules/auth.md) | api | yes | Optional. Explicit cookie domain (e.g. .x.com) for cross-subdomain sessions. Derived from BETTER_AUTH_URL when unset. It scopes both session cookies, client.session_token (signed in at /auth) and admin.session_token (signed in at /admin/auth); their names keep the two sessions apart. |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | [`api`](modules/api.md) | api | no | Required. Comma-separated allowed origins for credentialed cross-origin requests (e.g. https://app.x.com,https://admin.x.com). There is no localhost fallback: an origin outside this list gets no CORS headers. In dev, keep the localhost default here: pnpm env:setup runs pnpm dev:ports, which writes this checkout's real web, admin and app origins (localhost and DEV_HOST) into apps/api/.env.local, and that file wins. In production, list every deployed frontend (web, admin, app). |
| `DATABASE_URL` | [`database-postgres`](modules/database-postgres.md) | api | no | Postgres connection string, e.g. postgres://user:pass@host:5432/app. Read from apps/api/.env in local dev (saasaloy env, then pnpm env:setup) and from a Workers secret (`wrangler secret put DATABASE_URL`) in production. A HYPERDRIVE binding, when present, takes precedence over it. Unset with no HYPERDRIVE binding, `getDb` throws "No Postgres connection" on the first request and the route returns a 500. Add `?sslmode=verify-full` to the string for a remote database: postgres.js connects without TLS unless the string asks for it. |
| `EMAIL_FROM` | [`email`](modules/email.md) | api | required when `EMAIL_PROVIDER!=console` | Default sender address (e.g. hello@x.com), on a domain the selected provider is allowed to send from. Overridable per message. Required for every provider except `console`, which logs instead of sending and falls back to its own sender (`dev@localhost`) when EMAIL_FROM is blank. |
| `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | [`email`](modules/email.md) | api | no | Which installed provider sends: `cloudflare` (add email-cloudflare), `plunk` (add email-plunk) or `console` (add email-console). Always required — there is no default, so nothing sends by accident and nothing stops sending silently. |
| `KHUDEBARTA_API_KEY` | [`sms-khudebarta`](modules/sms-khudebarta.md) | api | required when `SMS_PROVIDER=khudebarta` | Required while SMS_PROVIDER=khudebarta, and may stay blank under any other provider. Khudebarta API key, from the Khudebarta portal under the account's API settings, issued together with the secret key. Read from apps/api/.env in local dev (saasaloy env, then pnpm env:setup) and from a Workers secret (`wrangler secret put KHUDEBARTA_API_KEY`) in production. Unset, every send through this provider throws SmsError("provider_error") before the request is built; set but wrong, the gateway rejects the send and it surfaces as SmsError("account_error") with providerCode "-66". |
| `KHUDEBARTA_API_URL` | [`sms-khudebarta`](modules/sms-khudebarta.md) | api | yes | Base URL of the Khudebarta gateway, without a trailing path. Optional: it defaults to https://portal.khudebarta.com:3770, and only an account Khudebarta assigned a different host or port needs to set it. It must use HTTPS. Cloudflare Workers strip a custom port from a plain `http://` subrequest, so an http URL with a port silently lands on port 80 and every send fails against the wrong service. The provider does not check this for you. |
| `KHUDEBARTA_SECRET_KEY` | [`sms-khudebarta`](modules/sms-khudebarta.md) | api | required when `SMS_PROVIDER=khudebarta` | Required while SMS_PROVIDER=khudebarta, and may stay blank under any other provider. Khudebarta secret key, issued in the Khudebarta portal alongside KHUDEBARTA_API_KEY. Read from apps/api/.env in local dev (saasaloy env, then pnpm env:setup) and from a Workers secret (`wrangler secret put KHUDEBARTA_SECRET_KEY`) in production. Unset, every send through this provider throws SmsError("provider_error") before the request is built; set but wrong, the gateway rejects the send and it surfaces as SmsError("account_error") with providerCode "-67". |
| `KV_KEY_PREFIX` | [`kv-upstash`](modules/kv-upstash.md) | api | required when `KV_PROVIDER=upstash` | Prefix put in front of every key `buildKey` produces (e.g. `staging:` or your project name). Required once KV_PROVIDER=upstash, and it must not be blank: one Redis database is one flat keyspace, so without a prefix `list` would scan every key in it and two environments sharing a database would collide. `createEnv` and `pnpm env:setup` both refuse a blank value. |
| `KV_KEY_PREFIX` | [`kv`](modules/kv.md) | api | yes | Optional prefix put in front of every key `buildKey` produces (e.g. `staging:`). Lets two environments share one namespace without colliding. Empty by default. |
| `KV_PROVIDER` | [`kv`](modules/kv.md) | api | no | Which installed provider stores values: `cloudflare` (add kv-cloudflare), `upstash` (add kv-upstash) or `memory` (add kv-memory). Always required — there is no default, so a deploy never silently swaps its store and a test run never silently reaches a real one. |
| `LOGGER_PROVIDER` | [`logger`](modules/logger.md) | api | yes | Which installed provider writes: `console` (add logger-console). Optional — unset selects the first registered provider, so logging works out of the box once one is installed; with no provider registered (a logger-only install) every log call is a silent no-op. Deliberately unlike EMAIL_PROVIDER: a naming typo throws, but a missing value never does, because an outage caused by the observability layer is worse than one absent knob. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | [`logger`](modules/logger.md) | api | yes | Minimum level to emit: trace \| debug \| info \| warn \| error \| fatal. Defaults to `info`; an unrecognized value falls back to it silently. |
| `PAYMENT_APP_URL` | [`payment`](modules/payment.md) | api | yes | The origin of the app a hosted checkout returns the payer to, e.g. https://shop.x.com. `create` refuses a returnUrl on any other origin. Optional; when unset, only http://localhost origins pass, which is the dev default. |
| `PAYMENT_PROVIDER` | [`payment`](modules/payment.md) | api | no | Which installed providers take payments, as a comma list in priority order: `console` (add payment-console), `manual` (add payment-manual), `bkash` (add payment-bkash), and `sslcommerz` (add payment-sslcommerz). `create({ method })` picks the first listed provider that offers the method. Always required: unset, empty or an unknown name throws when the client is built, so nothing takes real money by accident and nothing stops taking it silently. |
| `PLUNK_API_KEY` | [`email-plunk`](modules/email-plunk.md) | api | required when `EMAIL_PROVIDER=plunk` | Required while EMAIL_PROVIDER=plunk, and may stay blank under any other provider. Plunk secret key, the `sk_...` one from the Plunk dashboard under Project settings → API keys. It must be the secret key, not the public `pk_...` key, which cannot send. Read from apps/api/.env in local dev (saasaloy env, then pnpm env:setup) and from a Workers secret (`wrangler secret put PLUNK_API_KEY`) in production. Unset, every send through this provider throws EmailError("provider_error") before the request leaves the Worker. |
| `PLUNK_API_URL` | [`email-plunk`](modules/email-plunk.md) | api | yes | Base URL of the Plunk API, without a trailing path. Optional: it defaults to the hosted https://next-api.useplunk.com, and only a self-hosted Plunk instance needs to set it. It must use HTTPS (plain HTTP is accepted for localhost only) because the request carries PLUNK_API_KEY. Point it at a wrong host and every send fails with a 404 mapped to EmailError("provider_error"). |
| `PUBLIC_API_URL` | [`admin`](modules/admin.md) | admin | no | Origin the admin SPA calls for api and auth requests (e.g. https://api.x.com). Falls back to http://localhost:4000 in dev. The `PUBLIC_` prefix is what vite.config.ts exposes to the browser bundle. |
| `PUBLIC_API_URL` | [`app`](modules/app.md) | app | no | Origin the customer app calls for api and auth requests (e.g. https://api.x.com). http://localhost:4000 in dev. The `PUBLIC_` prefix is what vite.config.ts exposes to the browser bundle. The app's own production origin goes into CORS_ORIGINS, not here. |
| `PUBLIC_API_URL` | [`waitlist`](modules/waitlist.md) | web | no | Base URL of the api Worker the form posts to (defaults to http://localhost:4000 in dev). |
| `QUEUE_PROVIDER` | [`queue`](modules/queue.md) | api | no | Which installed provider runs background work: `cloudflare` (add queue-cloudflare) or `memory` (add queue-memory). Always required — there is no default, so nothing runs by accident and nothing stops running silently. |
| `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | [`storage-cloudflare`](modules/storage-cloudflare.md) | api | yes | Access key id of an R2 API token with Object Read & Write on the bucket, from R2 → Manage API tokens. The Worker binding is a different credential and cannot sign a URL, which is why this exists. Set it in `packages/env/.env` locally, run `pnpm env:setup`, and use `wrangler secret put R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` in production. |
| `R2_ACCOUNT_ID` | [`storage-cloudflare`](modules/storage-cloudflare.md) | api | yes | Cloudflare account id, from the dashboard URL or `wrangler whoami`. One of four optional values that together let this provider hand a browser a presigned URL. Leave them unset and reads and writes still work through the R2 binding — every upload and download just streams through the Worker's proxy route instead. |
| `R2_BUCKET_NAME` | [`storage-cloudflare`](modules/storage-cloudflare.md) | api | yes | Name of the bucket the S3-compatible URL addresses, e.g. `acme-storage`. It must be the bucket the `BUCKET` binding points at, or every presigned link answers `NoSuchBucket` while uploads still work. `apps/api/test/r2-bucket.test.ts` compares the two in `packages/env/.env` and `.env.prod`; a value only a remote source holds is not checked. |
| `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | [`storage-cloudflare`](modules/storage-cloudflare.md) | api | yes | Secret access key shown once when the R2 API token is created. A secret: never in wrangler.jsonc, never in a repo. `wrangler secret put R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in production. |
| `SMS_FROM` | [`sms`](modules/sms.md) | api | yes | Default sender for messages that don't carry their own `from` — an E.164 number, a short code, or an alphanumeric sender id, whichever the selected provider is allowed to send from. Optional: a provider routing through a pool or a messaging service assigns the sender itself. When it is unset and the message carries no `from`, a provider that requires a sender rejects the send with `invalid_message`. |
| `SMS_PROVIDER` | [`sms`](modules/sms.md) | api | no | Which installed provider sends: `console` (add sms-console) or `khudebarta` (add sms-khudebarta). Always required — there is no default, so nothing sends by accident and nothing stops sending silently. |
| `SSLCOMMERZ_MODE` | [`payment-sslcommerz`](modules/payment-sslcommerz.md) | api | yes | Which gateway host to use: `sandbox` for https://sandbox.sslcommerz.com or `live` for https://securepay.sslcommerz.com. Optional, and it defaults to `sandbox`, so a deploy that never set it cannot take real money; any other value fails the env check. |
| `SSLCOMMERZ_RECEIPT_EMAIL` | [`payment-sslcommerz`](modules/payment-sslcommerz.md) | api | required when `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=sslcommerz` | Required while PAYMENT_PROVIDER lists sslcommerz, and may stay blank under any other provider. A real mailbox you own, e.g. payments@yourdomain.com. SSLCOMMERZ requires cus_email on every session and mails its own receipt to it. A provider is handed an opaque payment reference and never learns the payer's address, so this is the one address it can name. |
| `SSLCOMMERZ_STORE_ID` | [`payment-sslcommerz`](modules/payment-sslcommerz.md) | api | required when `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=sslcommerz` | Required while PAYMENT_PROVIDER lists sslcommerz, and may stay blank under any other provider. Your SSLCOMMERZ store id, from the merchant panel: register a sandbox store at https://developer.sslcommerz.com, or use the live store SSLCOMMERZ issues you. Read from apps/api/.env in local dev (saasaloy env, then pnpm env:setup) and from a Workers secret (`wrangler secret put SSLCOMMERZ_STORE_ID`) in production. Unset, the provider reports `card` as unavailable and `create` answers method_unavailable; set but wrong, the gateway refuses the session and it surfaces as provider_error with the gateway's own failedreason. |
| `SSLCOMMERZ_STORE_PASSWORD` | [`payment-sslcommerz`](modules/payment-sslcommerz.md) | api | required when `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=sslcommerz` | Required while PAYMENT_PROVIDER lists sslcommerz, and may stay blank under any other provider. The store password issued with SSLCOMMERZ_STORE_ID, sometimes called the API password. It is sent on the session-open POST, on every validation call and on every refund, so a deployed Worker holds it as a secret (`wrangler secret put SSLCOMMERZ_STORE_PASSWORD`), never in wrangler.jsonc. |
| `STORAGE_IMAGE_TRANSFORMS` | [`file-uploads`](modules/file-uploads.md) | api | yes | Set to `true` when Cloudflare image transformations are enabled on the zone serving STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL. Default off, because the `/cdn-cgi/image/` prefix 404s on a zone that has not turned them on. With it off `publicImageUrl` returns the plain public URL and ignores its options, so every image still renders. |
| `STORAGE_PROVIDER` | [`storage`](modules/storage.md) | api | no | Which installed provider stores objects: `cloudflare` (add storage-cloudflare) or `memory` (add storage-memory). Always required — there is no default, so nothing writes to a real bucket by accident and nothing stops writing silently. |
| `STORAGE_PROXY_URL` | [`storage`](modules/storage.md) | api | yes | Absolute origin the proxy route answers on (e.g. https://api.x.com), for a caller on another origin. Optional: with it unset a proxy link is root-relative. |
| `STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL` | [`file-uploads`](modules/file-uploads.md) | api | yes | Origin a public object is served from — an R2 custom domain in production (https://files.example.com), or this api's own origin in dev. The object key is appended to it verbatim, so it holds an origin and never a path. Leave it unset and `POST /files/uploads` refuses `visibility: "public"` with a message naming this variable; nothing falls back to private. |
| `STORAGE_PURGE_AFTER_DAYS` | [`file-uploads`](modules/file-uploads.md) | api | yes | Days a soft-deleted row is kept before the sweep drops it. Defaults to 30. Read only by the sweep job, so it does nothing in a project without the `queue` capability. A value that is not a positive whole number throws on the first tick. |
| `STORAGE_URL_SECRET` | [`storage`](modules/storage.md) | api | no | HMAC key that signs the upload and download links the proxy route accepts. Required — nothing generates one. Make it with `openssl rand -base64 32`, put it in `packages/env/.env` for local dev and run `pnpm env:setup`, and set it in production with `wrangler secret put STORAGE_URL_SECRET`. |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | [`subscription-stripe`](modules/subscription-stripe.md) | api | required when `SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=stripe` | Your Stripe secret key (sk_test_… while you develop, sk_live_… in production). Required once SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=stripe. The client is built on first use, so a project that keeps SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=console runs the whole capability — sign-in included — with this unset; the throw then names the key on the first call that reaches Stripe. |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | [`subscription-stripe`](modules/subscription-stripe.md) | api | required when `SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=stripe` | Required while SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=stripe, and may stay blank under any other provider. The signing secret of the endpoint you registered at https://dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks, pointing at https://<your-api>/auth/stripe/webhook. The plugin verifies every delivery against it, so an unsigned POST is refused before any handler runs. |
| `SUBSCRIPTION_APP_URL` | [`subscription`](modules/subscription.md) | api | yes | Absolute https URL the subscription emails link to, normally your admin app's /subscription page. Also the one origin the checkout, portal and change-plan routes accept a redirect URL on. Optional; http://localhost:3001/subscription when unset, which is the dev default and is refused by the email renderer on any host but localhost. |
| `SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER` | [`subscription`](modules/subscription.md) | api | no | Which installed provider takes payments: `stripe` (add subscription-stripe) or `console` (add subscription-console). Always required — there is no default, so nothing charges a real card by accident and nothing stops taking payments silently. |
| `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` | [`kv-upstash`](modules/kv-upstash.md) | api | required when `KV_PROVIDER=upstash` | Required while KV_PROVIDER=upstash, and may stay blank under any other provider. REST token for the same database, from the same panel. Use the read-write token — the read-only one cannot `SET`, `DEL` or run the limiter's `EVAL`. Store it as a Workers secret (`wrangler secret put UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`), never in wrangler.jsonc, and rotate it in the Upstash console if it leaks. A wrong token surfaces as KvError("provider_error") with providerCode `401` and retryable false, because retrying a bad credential only burns request budget. |
| `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` | [`kv-upstash`](modules/kv-upstash.md) | api | required when `KV_PROVIDER=upstash` | REST endpoint of your Upstash Redis database, the `https://<name>-<id>.upstash.io` one from the database page under REST API. Required once KV_PROVIDER=upstash. Read from apps/api/.env in local dev (saasaloy env, then pnpm env:setup) and from a Workers secret (`wrangler secret put UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL`) in production. There is no default: unset, every call through this provider throws KvError("provider_error") before a request leaves the Worker. |
